title: Gate evidence (gates/<ID>.json)
description: Machine-readable gate evidence (tasks.md T005). Every object is closed and there is no free-form secret field: evidence records only booleans, status codes, byte lengths, pattern IDs, paths and hashes, never secret values, tokens, authorization headers, sensitive bodies or credential file contents. `provenance` binds the evidence to the environment it actually proved: the gate review (T024) uses it only while it still matches the current runtime/versions.yaml; otherwise the evidence is stale and the gate must be re-run.

backends.description: per-backend statuses, required where the gate is judged per backend (G9, G11, PRODUCTION-CONFORMANCE)

versions.description: Informational observed versions (for example Docker Engine and git). Not provenance: the review reads only `provenance`.

provenance.description: The environment this evidence proves (tasks.md, Global constraints: gate-evidence provenance). G0: the pins it observes and establishes. G6: the pins it establishes and the runtime_versions_digest of the post-G6 runtime/versions.yaml. Every other gate document: the runtime_versions_digest of the runtime/versions.yaml in force when it ran. Digest: 'sha256:' + hex SHA-256 of json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False) encoded as UTF-8.

inventory_inputs.description: G4 (tasks.md T015): the identity of the committed T014 artifacts this gate derived its matrix from - the T014 gate evidence, the control-plane host inventory and the trusted-allowlist draft. Each value is 'sha256:' + the SHA-256 of the file's exact bytes. G4 additionally requires all three to be git-tracked and clean when it starts. Host names are never hard-coded, so an intentional T014 revision remains possible: it re-runs T014, re-commits the inputs and re-runs G4, which rewrites these digests. What it prevents is an edit after the reviewed T014 state silently producing a different allow set.

network_policy_fingerprint.description: G4 (tasks.md T015): the digest of the global network-policy state the proof relied on. Canonicalization, in full, so launcher preflight and the T062 production re-check can recompute it: 'sha256:' + hex SHA-256 of json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False) encoded as UTF-8, where obj is {"global_network_rules": [...], "governance": {"active": <boolean>}}. global_network_rules contains one object per rule of `sbx policy ls --json` whose scope is "global" and whose resource_type starts with "network", each carrying exactly the fields id, name, scope, applies_to, resource_type, decision, resources, origin, layer, status, editable - resources sorted ascending - and the list itself sorted by each object's canonical JSON. Sandbox-scoped rules and run-scoped grants are excluded by construction, so they never move the digest. governance.active is the typed boolean read from `sbx policy check network <probe> --json`; an unread or non-boolean governance status yields no fingerprint at all rather than one hashed over a placeholder. The policy must be read with no sandbox-scoped network rule present, because the pinned sbx stops enumerating the global default-deny rule once one exists. It is read as a typed field: T024 propagates it into gates/eligibility.json and launcher preflight recompares it, so it is never parsed out of notes or evidence_ref prose.

proven_network_allowset.description: G4 (tasks.md T015): the destinations G4 actually proved permitted, per backend and profile. This is T051's input for generating runtime/policy/network.yaml and the set T061 checks membership against; both consume THIS typed field and never parse it out of notes prose. It is written only when G4 passes, so a set nothing verified can never reach a production policy.

observed_precedence.description: G1d (tasks.md T018): what each of the four adversarial runs ACTUALLY resolved to, as a typed field rather than prose, written whether the gate passes or fails, because T018 requires the observed precedence to be recorded either way and the fallback decision depends on which source won. Keys are the run labels: precedence-root and precedence-nested are the authoritative precedence proof, run under the managed settings V1 pins with the hostile copies present as candidates; lockout-root and lockout-nested repeat both contexts with managed strictPluginOnlyCustomization for skills and agents and are defense in depth only. Each entry records the identity of the exact Skill invocation, the SHA-256 of the body Claude was actually delivered, the trusted copy's SHA-256, the source classification, the marker names each delegated subagent reported, and the in-VM Claude Code build the pinned transcript shape was proven against. Only identity fields, digests, marker NAMES and PASS/FAIL facts appear: no transcript content, which holds unrelated tool inputs and outputs, is ever copied into evidence.

extraction.description: the sanitized in-VM extraction could not be read at all

claude_code_version.description: the in-VM Claude Code build whose transcript shape this observation is pinned to

skill_tool_use_id.description: the exact Skill invocation the delivered body was linked to by sourceToolUseID

verification_source.description: source classification from marker names: trusted-managed, hostile:<names>, or unclassified

trusted_body_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the trusted SKILL.md body (frontmatter removed) that the delivered representation must carry verbatim

expected_delivery_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the ONE representation the pinned build may deliver: the header naming the managed skill directory, a blank line, then the trusted body. delivered_sha256 must equal this

managed_skill_dir.description: the managed directory the trusted copy was installed in and read back from

observed_header.description: the header region Claude Code actually delivered, capped at 200 characters: a fixed phrase plus the directory it resolved the skill FROM. When a hostile copy wins, this names it. Never body content

subagents.description: per managed subagent, the identity marker NAMES its reply carried

prerequisite_restoration.description: G4 (tasks.md T015): present only when THIS run consumed a one-time, developer-authorized restoration of the documented post-G0 global network-policy baseline. It is run-bound: the run recorded the durable record's digest, the digest still matches the bytes on disk, and the baseline the run started from is the one the restoration produced. A later run that starts from an already-valid baseline omits the field even though gates/G4/prereq/restoration.json still exists, so a restoration claim is never inherited.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the durable restoration record's exact bytes

baseline_fingerprint.description: the fingerprint of the baseline this run started from

claude_subscription.description: G1a (tasks.md T016): what the Claude backend was actually proven to be, as a typed field rather than prose, written only when G1a passes. The plan and the fresh-sandbox property are recorded as the two SEPARATE observations they are. subscription_type_proven_at_login is the plan the step-1 sandbox reported after a real interactive login - a value the inherited-credential path provably never produces. subscription_type_reported_by_fresh_sandbox is what the completely fresh step-2 sandbox reported, recorded verbatim: it is null on that path, both before and after a successful execution, because the inherited credential carries the token without the plan metadata the login response cached. The null is never rewritten as the proven plan. proven_without_login and proven_without_api_key record that step 2 ran with no /login and with no provider API-key name set in its environment.

logged_in.description: the fresh sandbox reported an authenticated session

auth_method.description: the authentication mechanism the fresh sandbox used; a subscription login, never an API key

api_provider.description: the provider path the fresh sandbox used

subscription_type_proven_at_login.description: the plan step 1's real interactive login explicitly reported

subscription_type_reported_by_fresh_sand.description: what the fresh sandbox reported, verbatim; null on the inherited path

claude_code_version.description: the Claude Code build inside the pinned sandbox base that actually produced the result. It is informational: runtime/versions.yaml's claude_code pin describes the developer's HOST CLI, while the in-sandbox build is governed indirectly by the separately pinned sandbox_bases.claude digest (E14b).

docker_agent_version.description: the pinned Docker Agent artifact the G6 kit installed, read back from the VM

claude_secret_isolation.description: G1b (tasks.md T021): whether a PRIVILEGED repository workload inside the VM can read Claude's token material, as a typed field rather than prose, written on PASS and FAIL alike - because a FAIL here is a real, consumable result, not an absence of one. token_material_readable_by_privileged_workload true with implication 'trusted-only' is exactly T021's defined FAIL outcome: Claude stays a usable V1 backend but may only serve TRUSTED runs, and G9 consumes this rather than trying to overturn it. false with 'eligible-for-untrusted' is the PASS outcome, which still leaves G9 required. readable_findings names the CLASS of each finding and its count only ('home/claude-oauth-access x1'); no secret value, no file content and no digest of either ever enters the evidence, so the document stays safe to commit and read.

locations_scanned.description: the scopes the scanner covered, so a clean result states its own coverage

readable_findings.description: '<location>/<finding-class> x<count>' only - never a secret value

g0Provenance.description: G0: the exact pins it observes and establishes; compared field by field with runtime/versions.yaml (no digest, because G6 still adds pins after G0)

g6Provenance.description: G6: the pins it establishes, plus the digest of the post-G6 runtime/versions.yaml

digestProvenance.description: every gate document other than G0 and G6: the digest of the runtime/versions.yaml in force when the gate ran

hostList.description: bare lowercase hostnames, sorted ascending and unique

allOf.description: NOT-RUN always carries its reason (backend completion rule)
PARTIAL exists only for G11, until part B completes
G0 provenance records the pins it observes and establishes
G6 provenance records the pins it establishes and the post-G6 digest
every other gate document records the digest in force when it ran
a G0 PASS has recorded every G0 pin
a G6 PASS has recorded the artifact SHA-256 and both sandbox bases
G4 and production conformance record the machine-readable global network-policy fingerprint when they pass (T015, T062), so the gate review never parses it out of prose
only G4 can carry a prerequisite-restoration binding; no other gate restores the global network-policy baseline
a G4 PASS records the proven allow set as a typed field, and only a PASS may carry one
only G4 binds itself to the committed T014 inventory artifacts

a G1a PASS records the proven Claude subscription as a typed field, and only G1a may carry one: the plan comes from step 1's interactive login and the fresh-sandbox property from step 2, so neither is inferred from the other
